title: CROSSING BOUNDARIES: LEVERAGING SEMANTIC DIVERGENCES TO EXPLORE CULTURAL NOVELTY IN COOKING RECIPES
findings: The proposed textual novelty metrics showed significant correlations with the religious distance between countries. The paper's model explained religious distance better than other cultural distances (geographical, linguistic, etc.), with the 'Uniqueness', 'Difference', and 'Divergent Surprise' metrics having the most substantial effects. This suggests that textual divergences in cultural products like recipes reflect differences in religious backgrounds.

measurement_description: The paper measures the correlation between its proposed textual novelty metrics (derived from cooking recipes) and a pre-existing 'religious distance' metric between countries. This is done to validate that the proposed metrics can capture aspects of cultural difference, for which religious distance serves as a proxy.
